With a wave of his hand, the genie vanished, and Layla awoke the next morning, feeling different. She looked in the mirror and gasped—her long hair was now short, and she wore a boy's tunic. She was no longer Layla, but a boy named Layan.

He noticed how the world seemed different from a boy's perspective. He could run faster, climb higher, and even play with the boys without being told to sit quietly.

As the sun began to set, Layan returned to the cave, where the genie waited. "Thank you," he said, "for letting me experience life as a boy. I have learned that everyone has their own way of being, and that it's important to respect and understand each other."

The genie smiled. "You have grown wiser, Layan. Your wish has been fulfilled, and you will return to your true self."

With a final wave, the genie vanished, and Layan awoke back in his own body, still in the village. He smiled, knowing that he had gained a new understanding of the world and the people around him.
